title: Developer Experience Documentation Playbook: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, and Top Support Issues
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview

This playbook defines the standards, templates, and operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation at Redwood Inference focused on: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs site operating procedures, and the canonical list of top support issues and fixes. The goal is to ensure consistent, discoverable, and actionable documentation that reduces time-to-value for engineers, reduces support volume, and improves long-term maintainability.

Audience

- Primary: Software and ML engineers integrating Redwood APIs and SDKs.
- Secondary: Solutions engineers, support engineers, and technical writers.

Goals and success metrics

- Reduce first-time-success time for new engineers to < 30 minutes for a simple text-generation quickstart.
- Reduce repeat support tickets for SDK integration errors by 40% within 90 days of adoption of these templates.
- Keep core SDK guides and quickstarts covered by automated smoke tests in CI.

Document types covered

1. SDK Guides (language-specific reference + migration guides)
2. Quickstarts & Templates (minimal runnable examples + infra templates)
3. API Examples (patterns: streaming, function/tool calling, embeddings, retries)
4. Docs site operating procedures (content lifecycle, review, publishing cadence)
5. Top support issues and canonical fixes (triage playbooks & KB articles)

Standards & structure (all DevEx docs)

Every document must include:

- Short description (1-2 sentences).
- Intended audience and pre-reqs.
- Quickstart / TL;DR for instant success.
- Step-by-step examples with runnable commands.
- Configuration and compatibility table (SDK versions, API versions).
- Troubleshooting / top support issues.
- Ownership and reviewers.

Naming and file format

- Confluence page titles should be short and descriptive, use dashes for filenames in source JSON.
- Each generated JSON must include the metadata fields required by the confluence system (title, space, author, owner_team, status, created_at, last_updated).

SDK Guides: structure and best practices

Core structure for language SDK Guides (apply to JS, Python, Go, Java):

1. Overview and When to Use
2. Installation & Versions
3. Authentication (examples with env vars and KMS)
4. Quickstart (copy-paste runnable)
5. API reference snippets (common operations)
6. Error handling and retry patterns
7. Migration notes (compatibility table)
8. Examples & recipes (pagination, streaming, function calls)
9. Troubleshooting & top issues
10. Links: design docs, telemetry dashboards, backlog tickets

Example Quickstart (JavaScript)

- Prereqs: Node 18+, account API key.
- Install: npm i @redwood-inference/sdk

Code snippet (runnable):

export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-...
node quickstart.js

import Redwood from '@redwood-inference/sdk';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-1', prompt: 'Write a friendly greeting.' });
console.log(res.text);

Best practices (SDK guides)

- Surface minimal and idiomatic examples first (2-3 lines).
- Provide explicit guidance for auth rotation and local dev vs CI.
- Include pre-built config templates for common deployment patterns.
- Keep code snippets linted and runnable; CI should execute at least one quickstart per major release.

Quickstarts & Templates

Quickstarts are the fastest path to "hello world" and must be: minimal, runnable, and annotated. Each quickstart page must include:

- Objective (one sentence).
- Time-to-complete estimate.
- Prereqs and related quickstarts.
- Step-by-step instructions with commands.
- Expected output and verification steps.

Templates are slightly larger scaffolds (3-5 files) that show integration patterns (e.g., serverless inference proxy, webhook handler, embedding indexer). Provide a 1-click or copyable template and a short README.

Quickstart template example: Serverless text generation (Node + Vercel)

- Files: index.js, vercel.json, package.json, .env.example
- Commands:
  1. cp .env.example .env && edit REDWOOD_API_KEY
  2. npm install && vercel dev
  3. curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'

Configuration table (required)

| Template | SDK version | API version | Platform tested | Smoke CI job | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| node-vercel-textgen | 1.2.x | v1 | Vercel (local dev) | smoke-dev-textgen | devex-team |
| python-embed-indexer | 1.2.x | v1 | AWS Lambda | smoke-embed-indexer | devex-team |

API Examples: patterns & canonical snippets

Include canonical examples for common patterns:

- Text generation (sync & streaming)
- Chat messages (system/user/assistant roles)
- Function / tool calling examples (how to define tools and parse responses)
- Embeddings + vector search integration (indexing, batching)
- Reranking and log-prob inspection

Example (streaming pseudocode):

const stream = client.stream({ model: 'redwood-stream-1', prompt: 'Tell a story.' });
for await (const chunk of stream) { process.stdout.write(chunk); }

Retry and error handling patterns

- Use exponential backoff with jitter for 429/503.
- Surface specific SDK errors: AuthenticationError, RateLimitError, ModelUnavailableError.
- Provide per-route timeout recommendations: interactive UI routes: p95 < 500ms (where possible); batch jobs: per-request timeout 2m.

Docs site operating procedures (content lifecycle)

1. Drafting
  - Author creates page draft in Confluence space with the required metadata.
  - Link to related design docs and JIRA tickets.

2. Review
  - Request review from two reviewers: one peer engineer + one tech-writer.
  - Reviewer checklist: accuracy, runnable example verification, security review for secrets, accessibility (alt text), and concise language.

3. Publishing
  - CI checks run: eslint/md-lint for code blocks, smoke tests for at least one example, link-checker.
  - Author updates last_updated and sets status to published.

4. Post-publish maintenance
  - Quarterly content review reminders for high-traffic pages.
  - Flag pages for immediate update on breaking API/SDK changes.

Publishing checklist (must be completed before changing status to published)

- [ ] Title and metadata filled
- [ ] Quickstart verified locally or by CI
- [ ] Security/secret handling checked
- [ ] Reviewer sign-off (2 reviewers)
- [ ] Labels applied (standard: language, sdk, quickstart)
- [ ] Smoke test job associated in CI

Procedures: releasing SDK-compatible docs (numbered steps)

1. On SDK release branch, create or update corresponding SDK guide page and include migration notes.
2. Run docs smoke tests in CI; fix failing examples.
3. Get reviewer sign-off (engineer + devex tech writer).
4. Merge and set status to published and tag related release notes in product docs.

Top support issues and canonical fixes (canonical KB entries)

We track the top recurring support issues in the docs site so support engineers can link to a canonical fix. Each KB entry should include: symptom, root cause, reproduction, canonical fix, and postmortem action items.

Canonical issues (examples)

1) "401 / AuthenticationError after rotating API key"
- Symptom: SDK calls return 401 after key rotation.
- Root cause: Long-lived processes (celery, workers) not reloading env vars; API key cached in secret store credential provider.
- Canonical fix:
  1. Restart long-lived processes or reload credential provider.
  2. For k8s: update Secret and rollout deployment: kubectl rollout restart deployment/my-worker
  3. Add health-check that verifies authentication after credential rotation.
- Related KB: /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security

2) "High 429 rate for embeddings ingestion"
- Symptom: Bulk embeddings calls receive 429 or long queue delays.
- Root cause: Missing batching on client side and no retry with jitter.
- Canonical fix:
  1. Implement client-side batching (recommended: batch size 128 tokens/512 vectors depending on model).
  2. Use exponential backoff with jitter for 429 responses.
  3. Move heavy indexing to dedicated capacity jobs or schedule off-peak.
- SDK snippet (Python batch)

def chunked(iterable, n):
    for i in range(0, len(iterable), n):
        yield iterable[i:i+n]

for batch in chunked(items, 128):
    client.embeddings.create_batch(model='embed-1', inputs=[i.text for i in batch])

3) "Streaming client stalls or reconnects frequently"
- Symptom: UI partial responses, multiple reconnects.
- Root cause: Premature client-side buffer flush / timeout mismatch between proxy and client.
- Canonical fix:
  1. Increase proxy and client timeouts to allow streaming windows (suggested proxy idle timeout = 2m).
  2. Ensure Use of chunked transfer encoding and keep-alive.
  3. Add client-side incremental rendering that tolerates partial packets.

Triage playbook for new support tickets (quick, numbered)

1. Confirm reproduction steps with customer including SDK version and sample request.
2. Check telemetries: route, model, status codes, latency distribution (p50/p95/p99).
3. Search KB for matching symptoms; if found, return canonical fix.
4. If no KB match, escalate to devex on-call and capture reproducible minimal repro.

CI and automation requirements

- Every SDK repo must include a docs-smoke CI job that:
  - Runs the canonical quickstart (sanitizing secrets).
  - Validates example output against a golden assertion (non-deterministic parts can use regex).
  - Lints code blocks and markdown.
- A nightly job aggregates top support issues and ensures KB coverage for the 20 most frequent error signatures.

Ownership and contacts

- DevEx docs owner: devex-team@redwood.com (primary contact for doc workflows).
- On-call for urgent doc fixes: devex-oncall rotation (see eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts).
- SDK maintainers: each SDK repo must list a primary and secondary owner in the docs header.

Appendix: useful commands and examples

- Run local quickstart smoke test (Node example):

# set API key and run quickstart
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-test-...
node examples/node-quickstart/index.js

- Restart worker after key rotation (k8s):

kubectl set env deployment/my-worker REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-... --namespace=prod
kubectl rollout restart deployment/my-worker -n prod

- Minimal STACK config for template CI job (YAML)

jobs:
  smoke-docs:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: '18'
      - name: Install
        run: npm ci
      - name: Run smoke quickstart
        env:
          REDWOOD_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY }}
        run: node examples/node-quickstart/index.js

Appendix B: Template metadata table (for authors to copy)

| metadata_key | example_value | notes |
|---|---|---|
| title | node-vercel-textgen | short, dash-separated for filename |
| owner_team | engineering/devex | who maintains the template |
| sdk_version | 1.2.x | semver range tested |
| smoke_ci_job | smoke-dev-textgen | CI job name that verifies the template |
| platforms_tested | Vercel, Local | list of tested platforms |

Next steps / action items

- DevEx authors: adopt this playbook for all new SDK guides and quickstarts by 2026-09-30.
- Engineering managers: ensure SDK repos add a docs-smoke job in the next minor release.
- Support leads: nominate two canonical KB entries for consolidation into this playbook each quarter.
